cost_model_snapshot:
Assumptions used for committed-GPU cost model (shared 2026-02-26):

- Commit tiers requested by customer: 8, 16, 32 GPUs (NVIDIA A100 / H100-class).
- Example list price (negotiation baseline): $7,000/GPU/month at low commit. Stepped discounts assumed: 8 GPUs -> $6,500/GPU/mo, 16 GPUs -> $6,000/GPU/mo, 32 GPUs -> $5,400/GPU/mo.
- Performance assumption (conservative): one reserved GPU can sustain ~600 tokens/sec for their chosen 13B quantized inference profile (note: we flagged this as model/hardware dependent).
- Monthly tokens per GPU (theoretical): 600 tok/s * 3600 s/hr * 24 hr/day * 30 days = 155,520,000 tokens/month.
- Effective serving assumption (utilization): steady-state avg 55% utilization (to reflect diurnal and batch tails), peak headroom to 90% for minutes-long spikes.

Pricing worked example (8-GPU commit):
- Monthly committed cost: 8 * $6,500 = $52,000/mo.
- Tokens served per GPU @55%: 155,520,000 * 0.55 = 85,536,000 tokens.
- Tokens served by pool @55%: 85,536,000 * 8 = 684,288,000 tokens/mo.
- Raw infra cost per token = $52,000 / 684,288,000 = $0.000076 (7.6e-05) USD/token.
- Add infra & ops overhead (20%) => $0.0000912/token.
- Add platform/maintenance margin (10%) => $0.0001003/token (~0.010 cents/token).

Sensitivity notes:
- If utilization falls to 30% the effective $/token rises to ~ $0.000184/token. Break-even utilization to hit sub-$0.00010/token is ~45-50% for this price tier.
- At 16-GPU pricing ($6,000/GPU), same utilization (55%) => ~$0.000076/token after overhead and margin (approx 25% better than 8-GPU tier).
- Hosted-burst pricing (no commit) typically appears 2-3x higher per token but provides elasticity for market-open spikes; recommended hybrid: commit for steady base, route peaks to Hosted API.

Recommended commercial levers for negotiation:
1) Offer stepped discounts by commit band and 12-mo vs 6-mo term (e.g., additional 5% off for 12-month).
2) Include defined burst pool (hosted fallback) with throttles and accounting so procurement can see predictable overage cap.
3) Introduce utilization-based true-up clause: quarterly reconciliation with credits if utilization >95% (protects customer) or minimum utilization floor to protect Redwood economics.
4) Provide per-token examples for their exact workload (we requested sample traces from Halcyon to model accurately).

Risks called out: model perf variance (tokens/sec) has biggest impact on $/token; accuracy regressions if we push to more-quantized variants; procurement pushback on commit length.

Next deliverables from Redwood: revised pricing spreadsheet (tiered commit + per-token sensitivity), SLA draft with throughput guarantees and latency SLOs, POC runbook for 8-GPU pool (2-week synthetic + 1-week production mimic).
